summary: Seiji Kimura is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (attested 1986). He held posts at Komazawa University (attested 1990) and as a lecturer at Komazawa Junior College (attested 1995).
Specializing in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, Seiji Kumagai earned his PhD at Kyoto University (~2005–2008). He later served as an associate professor at Kyoto University (~2013).

Seiji Nemoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Meiji University (~1968–1978) and served as a professor at the University of Tsukuba (~2004–2015).
Seiji Tanaka studied under Bruno Petzold. He later held academic posts at Aoyama Gakuin University (~1961–1968) and Asia University (~1968–1976).
Seijun Ishii is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University from ~1977 to 1986. He later became a professor at Komazawa University (~2000).
A Buddhist studies scholar, Seikō Hirata studied at Kyoto University (~1948–1951) and under Shin'ichi Hisamatsu and Bokuo Seki. He held a post at Hanazono University from ~1954 to 1994.

Sein Tin studied at Basic Education High School No. 9 Mawlamyine, the University of Rangoon (~1917–1921), under Pe Maung Tin (1924–1927), and at Christ Church (~1927–1930), working in linguistics and other fields.

Seiran Ouchi worked in Buddhist and religious studies, founding Hoshi Sodan in 1874 and Meikyo Shinshi in 1875. He served as a lecturer at Nishi Hongan-ji and as president of Toyo University (1914–1918).

A Buddhist studies and Indology scholar, Seiren Matsunami studied at the University of Tokyo and under Walther Schubring and Naoshiro Tsuji. He held professorships at Kyushu University and Rissho University, and lectured at Taisho University.

A specialist in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology, Karashima studied at the University of Tokyo, Cambridge, and Peking University under several scholars. He held posts at the Eastern Institute and Soka University (~1994–2019).

A Buddhist studies scholar, Kato studied at Toyo University and Shingiyaha Daigakurin. He served as president of Buzan University, Taisho University, and Toyo University, and taught at the University of Tokyo and Rissho University.
A scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, Seitatsu Matsunami served as an assistant at the University of Tokyo and as a professor at Taisho University (attested 1992).

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology, Yanagida studied at Hanazono, Otani, and Kyoto Universities. He held long-term posts at Hanazono University, served as a professor at Kyoto University (1976–1986), and taught at Chubu University.

Specializing in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology, Sempa Dorje studied under Ram Shankar Tripathi. He held a professorship at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, attested between 1977 and 1998.
Sen Wang was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Peking University (~1931–1935). He later served as a professor at Minzu University of China (~1952–1982).

Senarat Wijayasundara is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. In 1999, he was attested as a teacher at the University of Kelaniya and a visiting lecturer at the Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore.
Senarath Paranavitana worked in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He succeeded Don Martino de Zilva Wickremasinghe and held a post at Leiden University (~1936–1937).

Senchu Murano was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1929–1933) and the University of Washington (~1934–1938). He later served as a professor at Rissho University (~1957–1978).

A scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, Mayeda earned degrees from the University of Tokyo and the University of Pennsylvania. He held posts at Pennsylvania, the University of Tokyo (1973–1991), and Musashino University (~1991–2001).

Senkei Sakawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his studies at Rissho University by 1965. He later served as a professor in the Department of Buddhism at Rissho University (attested 1981–1985).
